title: soapbar: verify_envelope_bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)
summary: Affected: soapbar. ### Impact `verify_envelope_bsp()` derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted `wsse:BinarySecurityToken`, validated **only** that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful `verify_envelope_bsp()` therefore proved only that the envelope was signed by *whoever supplied the embedded certificate* — never that it was signed by a *trusted* party. title: Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices
summary: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service to install malware on some customer routers and KVM devices, the maker of travel routers and remote-access KVM hardware said in a security notice updated today. The company identified and fixed the flaw on Friday and blocked the access the attacker used, so devices can no longer be infected through this route.
